chunks: And it was narrated from al-Qāsim, from Abān, from Abī al-ʿAbbās al-Faḍl al-Baqbāq, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Regarding a well into which a mouse, a beast, a dog, or a bird falls and then dies, he said: “It is taken out, then some buckets are drawn from the well; then one may drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) with it.”

key_terms.الدَّابَّةُ: a beast or animal falling into the well
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse falling into the well
key_terms.دِلَاءٌ: buckets of water drawn out as part of purification
key_terms.يَمُوتُ: dies in the well, causing the legal question
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: wudu (ablution) is performed with the water afterward
key_terms.يُخْرَجُ: it is removed from the well
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out from the well

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a mouse, dog, or bird dies in a well?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the purification of well water when an animal falls into it and dies. It states that after removing the dead animal and drawing out some buckets of water, the water may again be used for drinking and for wudu (ablution).
